svg.title: Australia wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: A continent-scale orientation places western, southeastern and island wine regions in their true relative positions. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Margaret River (WA). The southwestern corner of Western Australia, between maritime coastlines. 2: Barossa / Eden Valley (SA). Neighboring South Australian regions northeast of Adelaide. Eden Valley is generally higher and cooler. 3: Clare Valley (SA). North of the Barossa area, inland in South Australia. 4: McLaren Vale (SA). South of Adelaide near Gulf St Vincent. 5: Coonawarra (SA). Southeastern South Australia near the Victorian border. 6: Hunter Valley (NSW). Eastern New South Wales, north of Sydney and inland from Newcastle. 7: Yarra Valley (VIC). Southern Victoria, northeast of Melbourne. 8: Rutherglen (VIC). Northeastern Victoria near the Murray River and New South Wales border. 9: Tasmania. The island south of mainland Australia; one locator represents several widely separated vineyard districts.

g.text: Dots locate representative places · boundaries do not represent appellations
